title: What's Your Oriignal Idea?
author: rgrivera1113
selftext:
A lot of people are posting what amount to clones of existing games. Even I posted one like that. Granting that it was just a fun little experiment.

What original project are you working on?  I'm curious what people are working on that isn't a copy of something that already exists. If you don't want to share details, a couple of sentences will suffice.

I'll go first. My main project is a Professional Wrestling Territory Management sim. You build a territory by putting on shows that the audience cares about. The core loop is finished but it's pretty far from being a game. I've been working on it for about three months (mostly weekends). It's a passion project that I don't imagine would be particularly saleable. I'm making it because it's a subject that interests me and I think there's a lot of depth to it.

What are you guys working on?

replies.author: rgrivera1113
replies.body:
Ideas without execution will always be farts in the wind.  It's an interesting spot to be in where it's so much easier to execute an idea. It's a shame that so many people are using the tools to say, "Make Stardew Valley. Make no mistakes."

Having an idea is fine but making a game demands a hell of a lot more than a prompt of a vague idea.

comments.author: AlgaeNo3373
comments.body:
3D LLM visualizer/explorer of LLM neurons, poke them with words and see what lights up. It's in the vein of past work, but those games were mostly research tools and thus discontinued in pursuit of better methods as they arose. I doubt more than a handful would be interested in it and that's fine. I mostly work on it in my own time as a hobby rather than something I need to succeed commercially/critically. 

https://preview.redd.it/vjtdkzqvhjth1.png?width=1919&format=png&auto=webp&s=1c3e6c1f730343565d46081716177a9286184285

Not so much an original idea then, but a very niche thing that has no modern counterpart. Mostly, these things were built for people who already understood the systems, whereas mine is for total newcomers, so perhaps that part is where it's genuinely novel. 

And just to say: I'd *love* for someone to copy the idea (you're welcome to all the code/assets), make it a thousand times better, and have a huge commercial success with it. Then I wouldn't feel compelled to make it myself. They'd be doing me a huge favour. I just think this is an amusing inversion of many people's mentality here\~

comments.author: Nez_Coupe
comments.body: Mine will never ship, it’s just fun to make, but my idea is a scape-like meets the combat mechanic necessity of a souls-like. It’s also fully isometric and the map is fully divided into 40x40 tile subunits that function like little dioramas - camera zoom isn’t allowed, it’s a static view, and essentially you are a tiny sprite running around tiny assets fighting tiny enemies and skilling with tiny tools. Oh, and there’s a mysterious ether kinda stuff in the world and it glows different colors based on different factions/enemies use of it. Everything kinda revolves around this glowy stuff. It’s fantasy, but for instance the humans in the world use it power their structures and lives, and it glows cyan in the conduits of their building sprites. The Mycelian people (big ass mushroom humanoids that wear these fungal exoskeletons) power their suits with the energy, and it glows a fuscia/magenta color, which fades after you kill one and their carcass falls. Anyway, I’ve been vibing it in my downtime at work and home for gotta be 3 months now, and I have a TON of downtime at work, so I must’ve put a hundred (hundreds?) of hours into it. Most of my time is spent authoring the art, which I like to do myself now since I’ve gotten a lot better. It’s called Vaer. Which is the name of the energy in the world. There’s a bunch more but that’s the super long TDLR.
